key_insight: Reliable evaluation of engineered surfaces calls for hierarchical, multimodal NDE that combines rapid screening with calibrated confirmation.
engineering_relevance: Matching inspection physics to coating thickness, adhesion, residual stress, porosity, and interface defects can support component reliability and service-life decisions.
method: Review magnetic, electromagnetic, thermal, ultrasonic, optical, and X-ray inspection methods.
Link method capabilities and limitations to specific surface and interface problems.
Assess in-process sensing, data fusion, physics-informed machine learning, and digital twins.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a review of inspection capabilities and limitations, not a new experimental dataset or quantified performance benchmark.
watch_item: Limited probability-of-detection evidence, scarce reference specimens, and poor model transferability constrain qualification and deployment.
paper_title: Non-Destructive Evaluation for Engineered Surfaces: Methods, In-Process Sensing, and Data-Driven Inspection in the NDE 4.0 Era
